## Question and data

Is product-page browsing time associated with purchase differently for new and returning visitors? This initial report checks the data and describes observed patterns. It does not test the hypothesis or establish causation. Source: [UCI dataset 468](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/468/online).

Each row is one browsing session on an online retail site, collected over one year (Sakar et al., 2019). The 18 variables are page counts and seconds spent on administrative, informational, and product pages, Google Analytics bounce/exit rates and page values, the month, a weekend flag, technical and traffic codes, and visitor type. The outcome `Revenue` records whether the session ended in a purchase.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
d <- read.csv("data/online_shoppers_intention.csv")
stopifnot(nrow(d) == 12330L, ncol(d) == 18L)
```

## Overall checks

```{r overall}
cat("Sessions:", nrow(d), "\nVariables:", ncol(d),
    "\nMissing cells:", sum(is.na(d)),
    "\nPurchases:", sum(d$Revenue),
    "\nPurchase rate:", sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(d$Revenue)),
    "\nZero product-page duration:",
    sum(d$ProductRelated_Duration == 0),
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)", 100 * mean(d$ProductRelated_Duration == 0)), "\n")
```

## Data quality

```{r data-quality}
dup <- duplicated(d) | duplicated(d, fromLast = TRUE)
cat("Exact duplicate rows:", sum(duplicated(d)),
    "\nRows in duplicate groups:", sum(dup),
    "\nProduct pages in those rows:", paste(sort(unique(d$ProductRelated[dup])), collapse = ", "),
    "\nMax product duration in those rows:", max(d$ProductRelated_Duration[dup]),
    "\nPurchases in those rows:", sum(d$Revenue[dup]),
    "\nNegative durations:", sum(d[grep("_Duration", names(d))] < 0),
    "\nLongest product-page duration (hours):",
    round(max(d$ProductRelated_Duration) / 3600, 1),
    "\nSessions over 5 hours:", sum(d$ProductRelated_Duration > 5 * 3600),
    "\nLongest time per product page (minutes):",
    round(max(d$ProductRelated_Duration / pmax(d$ProductRelated, 1)) / 60, 1),
    "\nOne product page and zero duration:",
    sum(d$ProductRelated == 1 & d$ProductRelated_Duration == 0),
    "\nSessions with no pages of any type:",
    sum(d$Administrative + d$Informational + d$ProductRelated == 0),
    "\nPurchases with no product pages:", sum(d$Revenue & d$ProductRelated == 0),
    "\nMax bounce / exit rate:", max(d$BounceRates), "/", max(d$ExitRates),
    "\nSessions at that cap (bounce / exit):", sum(d$BounceRates == 0.2), "/",
    sum(d$ExitRates == 0.2), "\n")
```

There are no missing values or negative durations. The duplicated rows are all one- or two-page bounces with zero duration and no purchase; with this few variables, different sessions can look identical, so we keep them. The longest sessions have hundreds of product pages and the average time per product page never exceeds about 24 minutes, so we keep them and will check their influence with Cook's distance.

UCI says durations are updated when the visitor moves to another page, so the last page adds no time and most zero-duration sessions are one-page visits. Zero duration therefore means a short visit rather than no browsing, which is why we will test a zero-duration indicator.

Six sessions record no pages of any type, and six purchases have no product pages; we keep these 12 rows because they are too few to affect the fit. Bounce and exit rates never exceed 0.2 and pile up at that value, which looks like a cap, but neither is in our model. `Month` has no January or April sessions and spells out "June"; the model recodes it to "Jun" and orders months by calendar.

## Quantitative variables

Counts, center, and spread are on the original scales. Duration is skewed, so median and IQR should be read alongside mean and SD. `PageValues` is inspected here but is not a planned model predictor because its definition involves transaction value.

```{r quantitative}
quantitative <- c("Administrative", "Administrative_Duration", "Informational",
                  "Informational_Duration", "ProductRelated",
                  "ProductRelated_Duration", "BounceRates", "ExitRates",
                  "PageValues", "SpecialDay")
quant_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(quantitative, function(name) {
  x <- d[[name]]
  data.frame(Variable = name, Missing = sum(is.na(x)),
             Non_missing = sum(!is.na(x)), Mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
             Median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE), SD = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
             IQR = IQR(x, na.rm = TRUE))
}))
knitr::kable(quant_summary, digits = 3)
```

## Categorical variables

Operating system, browser, region, and traffic type are numeric *codes* and are treated as categories. The first table reports missingness; the second lists observed levels and counts.

```{r categorical}
categorical <- c("Revenue", "VisitorType", "Month", "Weekend",
                 "TrafficType", "OperatingSystems", "Browser", "Region")
cat_missing <- do.call(rbind, lapply(categorical, function(name) {
  x <- d[[name]]
  data.frame(Variable = name, Missing = sum(is.na(x)),
             Non_missing = sum(!is.na(x)))
}))
knitr::kable(cat_missing)

cat_levels <- do.call(rbind, lapply(categorical, function(name) {
  counts <- table(d[[name]], useNA = "ifany")
  data.frame(Variable = name, Level = names(counts), Count = as.integer(counts))
}))
knitr::kable(cat_levels)
```

## Visitor groups and analysis sample

The full-sample counts above include `Other`. The planned comparison uses only new and returning visitors, so the following tables show the exclusion explicitly.

```{r visitor-sample}
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(d$VisitorType)),
             col.names = c("Visitor type", "Sessions"))
analysis <- subset(d, VisitorType %in% c("New_Visitor", "Returning_Visitor"))
stopifnot(nrow(analysis) == 12245L)
cat("Analysis sessions:", nrow(analysis),
    "\nExcluded Other sessions:", nrow(d) - nrow(analysis), "\n")
visitor_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(analysis, analysis$VisitorType),
                                        function(group) {
  data.frame(VisitorType = group$VisitorType[1], Sessions = nrow(group),
             Purchases = sum(group$Revenue), Purchase_rate = mean(group$Revenue),
             Median_duration = median(group$ProductRelated_Duration),
             Zero_duration = sum(group$ProductRelated_Duration == 0),
             Zero_duration_share = mean(group$ProductRelated_Duration == 0))
}))
knitr::kable(visitor_summary, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Visitor type", "Sessions", "Purchases", "Purchase rate",
                           "Median duration", "Zero duration", "Zero share"))
```

```{r duration-plot, echo=FALSE}
boxplot(log1p(ProductRelated_Duration) ~ VisitorType, data = analysis,
        col = c("#85B6D9", "#E5A568"), xlab = "Visitor type",
        ylab = "log(1 + product-page duration)",
        main = "Browsing duration by visitor type")
```

## Observed purchase rates across duration

Zero duration is a separate group. The positive-duration cutpoints are the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles after pooling new and returning visitors with positive durations. Bounds are shown on the original data scale and rounded for display. For each visitor type and bin, the table and plot report the observed purchase rate with a pointwise 95% [Wilson score interval](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/prc/section2/prc241.htm). These summaries describe the observed rates. The proposed log-odds interaction requires a model-based test.

```{r duration-bins}
positive <- analysis$ProductRelated_Duration[analysis$ProductRelated_Duration > 0]
cuts <- as.numeric(quantile(positive, c(.25, .50, .75)))
stopifnot(length(unique(cuts)) == 3L)
analysis$Duration_group <- cut(
  analysis$ProductRelated_Duration, breaks = c(-Inf, 0, cuts, Inf),
  labels = c("Zero", "Positive Q1", "Positive Q2", "Positive Q3", "Positive Q4"))
rate_table <- aggregate(as.integer(analysis$Revenue),
  by = list(VisitorType = analysis$VisitorType,
            Duration_group = analysis$Duration_group),
  FUN = function(x) c(Sessions = length(x), Purchases = sum(x),
                      Purchase_rate = mean(x)))
rate_table <- data.frame(rate_table[1:2], rate_table$x, row.names = NULL)

cut_labels <- formatC(cuts, format = "f", digits = 2)
duration_bounds <- c("= 0", paste0("(0, ", cut_labels[1], "]"),
                     paste0("(", cut_labels[1:2], ", ", cut_labels[2:3], "]"),
                     paste0("> ", cut_labels[3]))
rate_table$Duration_bounds <- duration_bounds[as.integer(rate_table$Duration_group)]
```

```{r wilson-intervals, echo=FALSE}
z <- qnorm(0.975)
n <- rate_table$Sessions
p <- rate_table$Purchase_rate
denominator <- 1 + z^2 / n
center <- (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / denominator
half_width <- z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2)) / denominator
rate_table$Wilson_lower <- center - half_width
rate_table$Wilson_upper <- center + half_width

knitr::kable(data.frame(
  "Visitor type" = rate_table$VisitorType,
  "Bin" = rate_table$Duration_group,
  "Duration bounds" = rate_table$Duration_bounds,
  "Sessions" = n, "Purchases" = rate_table$Purchases,
  "Purchase rate" = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * p),
  "Wilson 95% CI" = sprintf("%.1f%% to %.1f%%", 100 * rate_table$Wilson_lower,
                            100 * rate_table$Wilson_upper),
  check.names = FALSE
))
```

```{r rate-plot, echo=FALSE}
bin_labels <- levels(rate_table$Duration_group)
plot_colors <- c("#2077A5", "#BD6C2F")
plot_symbols <- c(16, 17)
visitor_rates <- split(rate_table, rate_table$VisitorType)
y_ticks <- pretty(c(0, rate_table$Wilson_upper))
plot(NA, xlim = c(0.75, length(bin_labels) + 0.25), ylim = range(y_ticks),
     xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n", xlab = "Product-page duration group",
     ylab = "Observed purchase rate", main = "Purchase rates with Wilson 95% intervals")
axis(1, at = seq_along(bin_labels), labels = bin_labels)
axis(2, at = y_ticks, labels = paste0(100 * y_ticks, "%"), las = 1)
for (i in seq_along(visitor_rates)) {
  group <- visitor_rates[[i]]
  # Offset the two groups so both intervals are visible within each bin.
  x <- as.integer(group$Duration_group) + c(-0.09, 0.09)[i]
  arrows(x, group$Wilson_lower, x, group$Wilson_upper, angle = 90,
         code = 3, length = 0.04, col = plot_colors[i])
  lines(x, group$Purchase_rate, type = "b", pch = plot_symbols[i], col = plot_colors[i])
}
legend("topleft", legend = names(visitor_rates), pch = plot_symbols,
       lty = 1, col = plot_colors, bty = "n")
```

## Product-page count and browsing duration

The following checks use the same new- and returning-visitor analysis sample. The table cross-tabulates zero versus positive page counts and durations. Spearman's rank correlation summarizes their monotonic association on the original scales.

```{r count-duration}
count_duration <- with(analysis, table(
  "Product pages" = factor(ProductRelated > 0, labels = c("Zero pages", "One or more pages")),
  "Duration" = factor(ProductRelated_Duration > 0,
                      labels = c("Zero duration", "Positive duration"))
))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame.matrix(count_duration), row.names = TRUE)

zero_duration_with_pages <- count_duration["One or more pages", "Zero duration"]
total_zero_duration <- sum(count_duration[, "Zero duration"])
count_duration_rho <- with(analysis, cor(ProductRelated, ProductRelated_Duration,
                                         method = "spearman"))
```

Of the `r total_zero_duration` sessions with zero recorded duration, `r zero_duration_with_pages` (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * zero_duration_with_pages / total_zero_duration)`) recorded at least one product page. The count-duration Spearman correlation is `r sprintf("%.3f", count_duration_rho)`. This association motivates comparing duration-only and count-adjusted models before deciding whether to retain both predictors.

```{r count-duration-plot, echo=FALSE}
with(analysis, plot(log1p(ProductRelated), log1p(ProductRelated_Duration),
                    pch = 16, cex = 0.45, col = adjustcolor("#2077A5", alpha.f = 0.18),
                    xlab = "log(1 + product-page count)",
                    ylab = "log(1 + product-page duration)",
                    main = "Product-page count and browsing duration"))
```

## Hypothesis and baseline model

After adjusting for the controls below, the null hypothesis is that new and returning visitors have the same slope of `log1p(ProductRelated_Duration)` on purchase log-odds (interaction coefficient = 0). The two-sided alternative is that the slopes differ (interaction coefficient is nonzero).

The baseline logistic regression models `Revenue` using `log1p(ProductRelated_Duration)` and `VisitorType`, controlling for `Month`, `Weekend`, and `TrafficType`. Traffic types with fewer than 50 sessions in the analysis sample are pooled into one level. The proposal kept the product-page count (`ProductRelated`) only if its VIF with log duration is below 5; both GVIFs below are about 1.8, so it stays in the main model.

With $D_i$ the product-page duration, $\text{New}_i$ an indicator for new visitors, and $P_i$ the product-page count, the baseline model is
$$\text{logit}\,\Pr(\text{Revenue}_i = 1) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \log(1 + D_i) + \beta_2 \text{New}_i + \beta_3 P_i + \text{Month}_i + \text{Weekend}_i + \text{Traffic}_i,$$
where the last three terms stand for the dummy-coded control effects. The interaction model adds $\beta_4 \text{New}_i \log(1 + D_i)$, and $H_0: \beta_4 = 0$ versus $H_A: \beta_4 \neq 0$.

```{r baseline-model}
analysis$VisitorType <- relevel(factor(analysis$VisitorType), ref = "Returning_Visitor")
analysis$Month <- sub("June", "Jun", analysis$Month)
analysis$Month <- factor(analysis$Month, levels = intersect(month.abb, analysis$Month))
traffic_n <- table(analysis$TrafficType)
sparse_traffic <- names(traffic_n)[traffic_n < 50]
analysis$Traffic <- factor(ifelse(analysis$TrafficType %in% sparse_traffic,
                                  "Pooled", analysis$TrafficType))
cat("Pooled traffic types:", sparse_traffic,
    "\nSessions pooled:", sum(analysis$Traffic == "Pooled"),
    "\nPurchases pooled:", sum(analysis$Revenue[analysis$Traffic == "Pooled"]), "\n")

baseline <- glm(Revenue ~ log1p(ProductRelated_Duration) + VisitorType +
                  ProductRelated + Month + Weekend + Traffic,
                family = binomial, data = analysis)
car::vif(baseline)

main_terms <- c("log1p(ProductRelated_Duration)", "VisitorTypeNew_Visitor", "ProductRelated")
or_table <- exp(cbind(OR = coef(baseline), confint.default(baseline)))[main_terms, ]
knitr::kable(cbind(or_table, p_value = summary(baseline)$coefficients[main_terms, 4]),
             digits = 3, col.names = c("Odds ratio", "2.5%", "97.5%", "p-value"))
```

These odds ratios are adjusted associations from the baseline model, not the test of $H_0$.

Both models use the same 12,245 sessions, with returning visitors as the reference group. Both models include any retained quadratic log-duration term or zero-duration indicator. We will compare the models using a one-degree-of-freedom likelihood-ratio test and supplement it with a parametric bootstrap under the fitted model without the interaction.
